title.en: US Treasury’s Scott Bessent ‘will lose’ battle with bond markets, former mentor warns
title.zh: 美国财政部斯科特·贝森特“将输掉”与债券市场的战斗，前导师警告

summary.en: Billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller, former mentor to US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, has warned that Bessent's efforts to calm bond markets and lower borrowing costs are misguided. Druckenmiller advises Bessent to cut the budget deficit instead of attempting to suppress bond yields, suggesting Bessent is...
summary.zh: 亿万富翁投资者斯坦利·德鲁肯米勒（Stanley Druckenmiller）是美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特（Scott Bessent）的前导师，他警告称，贝森特平息债券市场和降低借贷成本的努力是错误的。德鲁肯米勒建议贝森特削减预算赤字，而不是试图压低债券收益率，并暗示贝森特目前的方法正在招致危险。

body.en: Trump ally should cut budget deficit rather than try to suppress bond yields, says billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Scott Bessent’s attempt to calm the bond markets and push down America’s cost of borrowing have attracted a rebuke from the US Treasury secretary’s former mentor. Billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller, who worked with Bessent at George Soros’s fund management firm in the 1990s, has warned that his former pupil is courting danger by trying to suppress US bond yields. Continue reading...
body.zh: 亿万富翁斯坦利·德鲁肯米勒·斯科特·贝森特表示，特朗普的盟友应该削减预算赤字，而不是试图抑制债券收益率。他试图安抚债券市场并压低美国的借贷成本，但此举遭到了美国财政部长前导师的谴责。亿万富翁投资者斯坦利·德鲁肯米勒 (Stanley Druckenmiller) 曾在 20 世纪 90 年代与贝森特在乔治·索罗斯 (George Soros) 的基金管理公司共事，他警告说，他的前学生试图压低美国债券收益率，这是在招致危险。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In the complex world of national finance, leaders like US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent face immense pressure to make decisions that affect millions. When his former mentor, Stanley Druckenmiller, offers a public rebuke and alternative strategy, it underscores the biblical principle that "where there is no guidance, a people falls, but in an abundance of...
reflection.zh: 在复杂的国家金融世界中，像美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特这样的领导人面临着巨大的压力，需要做出影响数百万人的决策。当前导师斯坦利·德鲁肯米勒公开批评并提出替代策略时，这强调了圣经的原则：“无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。” 这提醒我们，即使是最有权力的领导人，在应对经济挑战时，也能从多样化和经验丰富的谋士那里受益。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: ‘Enough is enough’: 121 Indigenous Victorians have died by suicide in the past five years
title.zh: “受够了”：过去五年，维多利亚州有121名原住民死于自杀

summary.en: In Victoria, 121 empty chairs were placed outside parliament to symbolize the Indigenous lives lost to suicide in the past five years. Despite a 2021 royal commission recommendation for First Nations healing centers, an Indigenous health service states the government has not funded these crucial facilities.
summary.zh: 在维多利亚州议会外，121把空椅子被摆放，象征着过去五年中因自杀而逝去的121名原住民生命。尽管皇家委员会在2021年建议设立原住民治疗中心，但原住民健康服务机构表示，政府尚未为这些关键设施提供资金。

body.en: Royal commission recommended First Nations healing centres in 2021 but the Indigenous health service says the state has ‘done nothing’ to fund it Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast On the steps of Victorian parliament stood 121 empty chairs, marking the number of Indigenous lives lost to suicide in the state in the past five years. All of these deaths, the state’s peak body for Aboriginal health said, came after the final report of the royal commission into mental health in March 2021 . Continue reading...
body.zh: 皇家委员会建议在 2021 年设立原住民康复中心，但原住民卫生服务部门表示，该州“没有采取任何行动”为其提供资金。 关注我们的澳大利亚新闻直播博客，了解最新动态 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 维多利亚州议会的台阶上摆着 121 张空椅子，标志着过去五年该州因自杀而丧生的原住民人数。该州原住民健康最高机构表示，所有这些死亡都是在皇家心理健康委员会于 2021 年 3 月发布最终报告之后发生的。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The tragic loss of 121 Indigenous Victorians to suicide in five years, marked by empty chairs, speaks to a profound communal despair. Like Elijah crying out 'It is enough' in his deepest anguish, this story reveals a community overwhelmed by suffering and a desperate need for the healing centers recommended in 2021. May Yahweh be near to those who feel life...
reflection.zh: 五年内121名维多利亚州原住民因自杀而悲剧性地逝去，这些空椅子象征着深刻的群体绝望。就像以利亚在极度痛苦中呼喊“够了”一样，这个故事揭示了一个被苦难压垮的社区，以及对2021年建议的治疗中心的迫切需求。愿雅伟亲近那些觉得生命过于沉重的人，愿实际的支持能为最需要的地方带来安慰和希望。

verse.textEn: He came to a broom bush, sat down under it and prayed that he might die. 'I have had enough, Yahweh,' he said. 'Take my life; I am no better than my ancestors.'
verse.textZh: 他自己在旷野走了一日的路程，来到一棵罗腾树下，就坐在那里求死，说：「雅伟啊，罢了！求你取我的性命，因为我不胜于我的列祖。」

title.en: Burnham plans trip to New York as Ukraine pleads for US-made missiles
title.zh: 伯纳姆计划前往纽约，乌克兰请求美国提供导弹

body.en: UK prime minister ‘likely’ to travel to US in September, after meeting Zelenskyy and saying supply problem is ‘fixable’ Andy Burnham has said he plans to travel to the US next month to join European leaders lobbying Donald Trump to supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles. The UK prime minister told Bloomberg he was “looking forward to going to New York” in September, which is when the UN General Assembly will meet. He said details of the trip were not “fully confirmed” but it was “likely” to go ahead. The trip would be Burnham’s first US visit since becoming prime minister in July. Continue reading...

reflection.en: In times of international crisis, leaders often seek collective wisdom and support to navigate complex challenges. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's planned trip to New York to join European leaders in lobbying for Patriot missiles for Ukraine reflects this principle. The proverb reminds us that a nation finds safety not in isolation, but through the...
reflection.zh: 在国际危机时期，领导人常寻求集体的智慧和支持，以应对复杂的挑战。英国首相安迪·伯纳姆计划前往纽约，与欧洲领导人一同游说为乌克兰提供“爱国者”导弹，正体现了这一原则。这句箴言提醒我们，一个国家并非孤立无援，而是在众多谋士的智慧和为和平安全共同努力的合作中找到安全。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

Luke Harding's career, reporting from challenging locations like Kyiv and Moscow, exemplifies the diligent pursuit of understanding complex global events. In a world grappling with the war in Ukraine and geopolitical shifts, the opportunity for readers...

title.en: Lockerbie bombing trial postponed days before it was due to start
title.zh: 洛克比空难审判在开庭前几天被推迟

summary.en: The trial of a Libyan man is delayed for a third time, after new evidence on the 37-year-old case came to light three days ago.
summary.zh: 一名利比亚男子的审判第三次被推迟，此前关于这起37年前案件的新证据于三天前浮出水面。

body.en:
The trial of a Libyan man over the Lockerbie bombing has been postponed for a third time, after new evidence on the 37-year-old case came to light three days ago.

Jury selection was due to get under way in Washington DC on Wednesday but the BBC understands a new start date has been set for January next year.

Lawyers acting for Abu Agila Mohammad Kheir Al-Marimi said "newly discovered evidence" previously unknown to the defence and prosecutors from the US government emerged on Friday 21 August.

Al-Marimi has denied building the bomb that destroyed Pan Am Flight 103 on December 21, 1988, killing 270 people.

His lawyers told the court: "Constitutional and ethical obligations require the defence to investigate this development."

They said they met Al-Marimi on Sunday and he agreed that they should ask for the postponement.

The trial judge, Dabney Friedrich, has agreed that the start date should be set aside, underlining the potential importance of the new evidence.

She would have been extremely reluctant to allow an 11th hour postponement after months of preparation and marathon pre-trial legal battles.

For the relatives of those who died and Al-Marimi himself, this latest delay means a verdict might not come until next spring.

It is yet another stunning development in a saga that has witnessed countless twists and turns over nearly four decades.

Pan Am 103 was flying from Heathrow to New York when the bomb exploded in its forward hold, breaking the plane apart at 31,000 feet.

All 259 passengers and crew on board were killed. Another 11 people died in Lockerbie when the wreckage fell on their homes.

Nearly four decades later, the bombing remains the worst terror attack and mass murder in British history.

Al-Marimi has been in US custody since 2022 and was originally due to stand trial in May 2025.

That date was set aside following a joint request from the prosecution and defence, who cited the complexity of the case and Al-Marimi's ill health.

The trial was pencilled in for April this year but was called off again, after the defence asked for more time to prepare.

The Lockerbie bombing has been the subject of a joint Scottish-US investigation since December 1988.

Prosecutors from the Crown Office and detectives from Police Scotland were due to travel to Washington to attend the case, and Scottish witnesses were expected to be among the first to give evidence at the trial.

Laura Buchan, head of the Lockerbie investigation team at the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service said: "I recognise that this adjournment will be disappointing for the families and for those who have followed this case over many years.

"As the matter remains before the court, it would not be appropriate to comment on the reasons for the adjournment. Although...
body.zh: 三天前，有关这起 37 年前案件的新证据曝光后，对一名利比亚男子洛克比爆炸案的审判已第三次推迟。 陪审团遴选原定于周三在华盛顿特区开始，但 BBC 获悉，新的开始日期已定于明年 1 月。 Abu Agila Mohammad Kheir Al-Marimi 的代理律师表示，美国政府的辩方和检察官此前不知道的“新发现的证据”于 8 月 21 日星期五出现。 Al-Marimi 否认制造了 1988 年 12 月 21 日摧毁泛美 103 航班、造成 270 人死亡的炸弹。 他的律师告诉法庭：“宪法和道德义务要求辩方调查这一事态发展。” 他们说他们周日会见了阿尔马里米，他同意他们应该要求推迟。 主审法官达布尼·弗里德里希 (Dabney Friedrich) 同意推迟开始日期，强调了新证据的潜在重要性。 经过数月的准备和马拉松式的审前法律斗争后，她非常不愿意允许推迟 11 个小时。 对于死者亲属和阿尔马里米本人来说，最新的延误意味着判决可能要到明年春天才能做出。 这是近四十年来经历了无数曲折的传奇故事中又一个令人惊叹的发展。 泛美 103 班机正从希思罗机场飞往纽约时，炸弹在前舱爆炸，飞机在 31,000 英尺的高度解体。 机上259名乘客和机组人员全部遇难。洛克比空难中另有 11 人因飞机残骸落在他们的房屋上而丧生。 近四十年后，这起爆炸事件仍然是英国历史上最严重的恐怖袭击和大规模谋杀。 Al-Marimi 自 2022 年以来一直被美国拘留，原定于 2025 年 5 月接受审判。 在控方和辩方的联合请求下，这一日期被搁置，控方称案件十分复杂，而且 Al-Marimi 的健康状况不佳。 该审判原定于今年四月举行，但在辩方要求更多时间准备后再次被取消。 自 1988 年 12 月以来，洛克比爆炸事件一直是苏格兰和美国联合调查的对象。 英国皇家办公室的检察官和苏格兰警察局的侦探将前往华盛顿出席此案，预计苏格兰证人将成为首批在审判中提供证据的人之一。 英国皇家办公室和检察官财政局洛克比调查小组负责人劳拉·巴肯 (Laura Buchan) 表示：“我认识到，这次休庭会让受害者家属和多年来关注此案的人感到失望。” “由于此事仍在法庭审理中，因此不宜对延期的原因发表评论。虽然...

reflection.en: After 37 years, the Lockerbie bombing trial faces another delay due to newly discovered evidence, reminding us that the pursuit of truth can be a long and arduous journey. Proverbs 18:15 speaks to the value of an intelligent heart that acquires knowledge and a wise ear that seeks it. Even decades later, the legal system continues its diligent search for all...
reflection.zh: 洛克比空难审判在37年后因新证据的出现而再次推迟，这提醒我们，寻求真相可能是一段漫长而艰辛的旅程。箴言18:15谈到有悟性的心获得知识，智慧的耳寻求知识的价值。即使在几十年后，司法系统仍在勤奋地搜寻所有可用的事实，以确保为270名受害者伸张正义。

verse.textEn: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, for the ears of the wise seek it out.
verse.textZh: 聪明人的心得知识；智慧人的耳求知识。

title.en: Iran says it is 'fully prepared' to counter widened US economic sanctions
title.zh: 伊朗称已“充分准备”应对美国扩大经济制裁

summary.en: The US calls its latest sanctions on Iran an "economic D-Day", but Tehran says it has a plan to address them.
summary.zh: 美国称其对伊朗的最新制裁为“经济诺曼底登陆日”，但德黑兰表示已制定计划应对。

body.en:
Iran has said it is confident it can counter widened US sanctions after Washington announced what it described as an "economic D-Day" against the country to try to isolate it from the global economy.

Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran was "fully prepared" for the sanctions, which he said would lead to "another defeat" for the US.

Announcing a raft of new measures, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said any nation financially partnering with Iran would be isolated, and that banks and businesses dealing with Iran would share its isolation if they refused to cut ties.

The moves follow U-turns and extended deadlines from the White House in its efforts to end the conflict.

Bessent described the measures as "the single greatest financial offensive ever" against Iran, which would "tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue".

Iran's largest trading partners include China, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates – which announced last week it was halting all trade and financial transactions with Tehran.

But hours after the US announcement, Iran said it was confident its trading partners would continue to do business.

Madanizadeh said neither China nor Russia had accepted the US measures, and predicted other countries would resist them.

"The government is and was ready and has a two-year plan to manage these events," he told state television, adding Tehran had been "waiting for these plans for a long time".

The Chinese Foreign Ministry said sanctions and pressure tactics did not help and Beijing would do what was necessary to protect China's interests.

The war has led to hikes in global oil prices, and in response to the latest threat Iran warned it would shut down all oil exports from the region if the war continued.

The Iranian regime has also issued a fresh warning to ships not to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without permission, according to Reuters.

One fifth of the world's oil and gas usually passes through the strait - a narrow waterway south of Iran. But the flow has been effectively blocked by the country since the conflict began at the end of February, leading to higher oil prices globally.

At a press conference earlier on Monday outlining what has been called "Operation Economic Outcast", Bessent said the US was launching an "economic onslaught against Iran's financial connections around the globe".

"Iran now faces a very clear choice with only two paths before them: complete global isolation... or a path back to normalcy with an opportunity to rejoin the global economy," he said.

The treasury secretary claimed America was "no longer managing the Iranian threat, we are ending it".

Bessent said the Treasury had mapped networks, facilitators and financial channels used by Iran to evade sanctions...
body.zh: 伊朗表示，在华盛顿宣布对伊朗实施所谓的“经济诺曼底登陆”以试图将其与全球经济隔离之后，它有信心能够反击美国扩大的制裁。 伊朗经济部长阿里·马达尼扎德表示，德黑兰已为制裁“做好充分准备”，他表示这将导致美国“又一次失败”。 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特宣布了一系列新措施，表示任何与伊朗进行金融合作的国家都将被孤立，而与伊朗打交道的银行和企业如果拒绝切断关系，也将受到同样的孤立。 这些举措是在白宫为结束冲突而做出的180度大转变并延长最后期限之后采取的。 贝森特将这些措施描述为针对伊朗的“有史以来最大规模的金融攻势”，这将“收紧绞索并封锁每一个潜在的收入来源”。 伊朗最大的贸易伙伴包括中国、土耳其和阿拉伯联合酋长国，后者上周宣布停止与德黑兰的所有贸易和金融交易。 但在美国宣布这一消息几小时后，伊朗表示有信心其贸易伙伴将继续开展业务。 马达尼扎德表示，中国和俄罗斯都没有接受美国的措施，并预计其他国家会抵制这些措施。 他对国家电视台表示：“政府已经做好准备，并制定了一个两年计划来管理这些事件。”他补充说，德黑兰已经“等待这些计划很长时间了”。 中国外交部表示，制裁和施压策略无济于事，北京将采取必要措施保护中国利益。 战争导致全球石油价格上涨，为了应对最新的威胁，伊朗警告称，如果战争继续下去，它将关闭该地区的所有石油出口。 据路透社报道，伊朗政权还向船只发出新警告，不得未经许可通过霍尔木兹海峡。 世界上五分之一的石油和天然气通常经过该海峡——伊朗南部的一条狭窄水道。但自2月底冲突爆发以来，石油流动已被该国有效阻断，导致全球油价上涨。 在周一早些时候举行的新闻发布会上，贝森特概述了所谓的“经济放逐行动”，称美国正在“对伊朗在全球的金融联系发动经济攻击”。 他说：“伊朗现在面临一个非常明确的选择，摆在他们面前的只有两条路：完全的全球孤立……或者恢复正常并有机会重新加入全球经济。” 财政部长声称美国“不再应对伊朗威胁，我们正在结束它”。 贝森特表示，财政部已经绘制了伊朗用来逃避制裁的网络、协助者和金融渠道……

reflection.en: The news reports both the US and Iran expressing confidence in their respective plans regarding economic sanctions, with Tehran declaring itself "fully prepared" to counter what Washington calls an "economic D-Day." In a world where nations strategize and declare their readiness, Proverbs 16:3 reminds us that human plans find their true establishment when...
reflection.zh: 新闻报道称，美国和伊朗都对其各自的经济制裁计划充满信心，德黑兰表示已“充分准备”应对华盛顿所称的“经济诺曼底登陆日”。在一个国家制定战略并宣称其准备就绪的世界里，箴言16:3提醒我们，人类的计划若要真正得以确立，需要将其交托给雅伟。这一视角邀请我们思考，超越我们自身的智慧或力量，成功的最终来源和稳定之本是什么。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Songs created by AI banned from Australia's music charts
title.zh: 澳大利亚音乐排行榜禁止人工智能创作的歌曲

summary.en: Australia's music industry has banned songs largely or wholly created by AI from its charts, aiming to "promote the human nature of artistry" after an AI-remixed Madonna song topped the dance charts.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚音乐行业已禁止主要或完全由人工智能创作的歌曲进入其排行榜，此举旨在“促进艺术的人性本质”，此前一首由人工智能混音的麦当娜歌曲曾登上舞曲榜榜首。

body.en:
Songs that are largely or wholly created by AI have been banned from Australia's music charts.

The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) said the new code would help "promote the human nature of artistry".

It follows a controversy around a cover of Madonna's Like A Prayer by Australian DJ Josh Fawaz which recently topped the ARIA dance singles chart and peaked at number 2 on the country's overall chart.

The song has become a staple of commercial radio station playlists and been streamed more than 48 million times on Spotify alone.

ARIA said that Australian artists were competing for attention "in the most crowded market in history" and that it was "not interested in promoting or celebrating the success of AI-generated music that does not contain human artistry".

Under the new rules, AI assistance can still be used, but humans must have written the song, and have performed the lead vocal and primary instruments.

AI can also still be used for mastering songs and, for example, using drum machines and auto tune.

Earlier this year a song was banned from Sweden's music charts because it was created by AI.

And in July, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) said AI guidelines would be rolled out in Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia for use in their official charts.

The updated code, based on the IFPI directive, also excludes music that raises "stream or chart manipulation concerns".

ARIA chief executive Annabelle Herd said: "These changes reflect our intent to remain dynamic and promote the human nature of artistry in what is, to say the least, a rapidly developing space."

"Artists already use AI tools in their work, the charts can and should evolve to keep room for that, but music generated wholesale by services built on artists' recordings is a different matter."

She added: "A chart that rewards unlicensed AI output would undercut the very basis of the recorded music we exist to represent."

Artists will be required to declare AI use when they submit a song for chart consideration.

ARIA said that if it later emerged music was largely AI-generated it could retrospectively adjust chart positions, and if the piece topped the charts, it may request that awards given for reaching Number One were returned.

Last month, they shared an AI-assisted version of their 2014 hit High on Instagram, captioned: "When you re-record your own song with AI so Australian radio will play it."

Band member Adam Hyde told Channel Nine's Today show that AI-generated music was "removing the human experience from life".

In July this year, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese promised "the strongest possible protection" from AI for Australian creatives.

body.zh: 大部分或完全由人工智能创作的歌曲已被禁止出现在澳大利亚音乐排行榜上。 澳大利亚唱片工业协会（ARIA）表示，新准则将有助于“促进艺术的人性化”。 此前，澳大利亚 DJ Josh Fawaz 翻唱了麦当娜的《Like A Prayer》引发争议，该歌曲最近登上了 ARIA 舞曲单曲榜榜首，并在该国总体排行榜上排名第二。 这首歌已成为商业广播电台播放列表的主要内容，仅在 Spotify 上的播放量就超过 4800 万次。 ARIA 表示，澳大利亚艺术家正在“在历史上最拥挤的市场”中争夺注意力，并且“对推广或庆祝不包含人类艺术性的人工智能生成音乐的成功不感兴趣”。 根据新规则，仍然可以使用人工智能辅助，但歌曲必须由人类创作，并演奏主唱和主要乐器。 人工智能仍然可以用于掌握歌曲，例如使用鼓机和自动调音。 今年早些时候，瑞典音乐排行榜禁止一首歌曲，因为它是由人工智能创作的。 7 月，国际唱片业联合会 (IFPI) 表示，人工智能指南将在拉丁美洲、中东、非洲和东南亚推出，用于其官方排行榜。 更新后的代码基于 IFPI 指令，还排除了引发“流媒体或图表操纵问题”的音乐。 ARIA 首席执行官安娜贝尔·赫德 (Annabelle Herd) 表示：“这些变化反映了我们在这个快速发展的领域保持活力并提升艺术人性的意图。” “艺术家已经在他们的工作中使用人工智能工具，图表可以而且应该不断发展以为此留出空间，但通过基于艺术家录音的服务批量生成的音乐是另一回事。” 她补充道：“奖励未经许可的人工智能输出的图表将削弱我们所代表的录制音乐的基础。” 艺术家在提交歌曲供排行榜考虑时将被要求声明人工智能的使用。 ARIA 表示，如果后来发现音乐主要是由人工智能生成的，它可以回顾性地调整排行榜位置，如果这首作品名列榜首，它可能会要求退回为达到第一名而颁发的奖项。 上个月，他们在 Instagram 上分享了 2014 年热门歌曲《High》的人工智能辅助版本，标题是：“当你用人工智能重新录制自己的歌曲时，澳大利亚电台就会播放它。” 乐队成员亚当·海德 (Adam Hyde) 在第九频道的《今日》节目中表示，人工智能生成的音乐正在“消除人类的生活体验”。 今年 7 月，澳大利亚总理 Anthony Albanese 承诺为澳大利亚创意人员提供“尽可能最强的保护”，使其免受人工智能的侵害。 阿尔巴尼斯承诺作家和音乐家将...

reflection.en: The Australian Recording Industry Association's decision to ban AI-generated songs from its charts highlights a growing conversation about the unique value of human creativity. In a world increasingly shaped by technology, this move to "promote the human nature of artistry" reminds us that our capacity to create, innovate, and express is a profound...
reflection.zh: 澳大利亚唱片业协会禁止人工智能创作歌曲进入排行榜的决定，凸显了关于人类创造力独特价值日益增长的讨论。在一个日益受科技塑造的世界里，这项旨在“促进艺术人性本质”的举措提醒我们，我们创造、创新和表达的能力，深刻反映了我们是按一位有创造力的雅伟的形象所造。它鼓励我们珍视并培养只有人类艺术家才能提供的独特贡献。

verse.textEn: So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
verse.textZh: 神就照着自己的形象造人，乃是照着他的形象造男造女。

title.en: UK drone factories may face attacks from 'unknown sources', says Kremlin adviser
title.zh: 克里姆林宫顾问称，英国无人机工厂可能面临“不明来源”的袭击

summary.en: A Kremlin adviser suggested that UK drone factories might face "semi-military" attacks from "unknown sources" after the UK announced it would share blueprints for missile components with Ukraine. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham plans to travel to the US to lobby for Ukraine's defense needs.
summary.zh: 克里姆林宫一位顾问表示，在英国宣布将向乌克兰提供英国制造的导弹部件蓝图后，英国无人机工厂可能面临“不明来源”的“半军事”袭击。英国首相安迪·伯纳姆计划前往美国，游说美国总统特朗普支持乌克兰的国防需求。

body.en:
Andrei Fedorov, an adviser to the Kremlin, says there might be a "semi-military" response against UK drone factories by "unknown sources" over the sharing of blueprints for British-made cruise missile components .

His comments on BBC Newsnight come as UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he plans to travel to the US next month with European leaders to lobby US President Trump on Ukraine's defence needs.

He said that while the details were not "fully confirmed", it is "likely" he will go. The trip would be his first to the US since becoming prime minister in July.

"Leaving today, I'm quite clear what I need to do in the next few weeks," he said following his official visit to Ukraine on Monday, during which he promised to continue pressuring Russia.

The UK has also agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile , a French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile. The blueprints will allow Ukraine to produce the long-range weapon domestically.

Fedorov, who is Russia's former deputy foreign minister, said Putin was facing "serious" pressure "to undertake certain measures against UK". Asked on BBC Newsnight where the pressure was coming from, Fedorov responded, "public opinion polls, it's coming from journalists, from mass media".

Asked what a "semi-military" response might look like, Fedorov said "it could take the form of something might happen with enterprises, with factories which are producing drones for Ukraine."

The comments are in line with those made by Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Monday, when he criticised the UK's decision to share the missile blueprints. Peskov said it prevented "even the slightest progress" towards achieving peace.

He told reporters on Monday that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate any missile production sites to destroy them.

"Britain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire," he added.

In response, Burnham said: "Who started the fire? That's the question, isn't it?"

Burnham's visit to Ukraine was his first official international visit. He met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv and chaired his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing", set up by the UK and France under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

Burnham has been reaffirming the UK's support for Ukraine in the wake of escalating Russian strikes in recent weeks - including one last week on a shopping centre that killed at least 16 people.

Ukraine has been relying on American supplies of the Patriot interceptor missiles, which are used to combat Russia's ballistic missiles , but stockpiles are running low due to the war in Iran, leaving Ukraine vulnerable to Russian attacks.

body.zh: 克里姆林宫顾问安德烈·费多罗夫表示，“不明来源”可能会因分享英国制造的巡航导弹组件的蓝图而对英国无人机工厂做出“半军事”反应。 他在英国广播公司新闻之夜发表评论之际，英国首相安迪·伯纳姆表示，他计划下个月与欧洲领导人一起前往美国，就乌克兰的国防需求游说美国总统特朗普。 他说，虽然细节尚未“完全确认”，但他“很可能”会去。这是他自七月就任总理以来首次访问美国。 “今天离开，我很清楚接下来几周需要做什么，”他在周一对乌克兰进行正式访问后表示，期间他承诺将继续向俄罗斯施压。 英国还同意移交英国制造的“头皮”导弹零部件的设计图，该导弹是英国“风暴之影”巡航导弹的法国版本。该蓝图将使乌克兰能够在国内生产远程武器。 俄罗斯前副外长费多罗夫表示，普京面临“严重”压力，“要求其对英国采取某些措施”。当被问及英国广播公司新闻之夜的压力来自哪里时，费多罗夫回答说：“民意调查，它来自记者，来自大众媒体”。 当被问及“半军事”回应可能会是什么样子时，费多罗夫表示，“这可能会发生在为乌克兰生产无人机的企业和工厂身上。” 这些言论与克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫周一的言论一致，当时他批评了英国分享导弹蓝图的决定。佩斯科夫表示，这阻碍了实现和平的“哪怕是最轻微的进展”。 他周一告诉记者，俄罗斯军方已经在收集数据，以确定任何导弹生产基地的位置，以摧毁它们。 “英国站在基辅政权一边卷入这场战争。英国有条不紊、定期火上浇油，”他补充道。 伯纳姆回应道：“谁放火了？这就是问题所在，不是吗？” 伯纳姆对乌克兰的访问是他首次正式国际访问。他在基辅会见了乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基，并主持了由英国和法国在其前任凯尔·斯塔默爵士领导下成立的“自愿联盟”的第一次会议。 在俄罗斯最近几周不断升级的袭击事件之后，伯纳姆一直重申英国对乌克兰的支持，其中包括上周针对一家购物中心的袭击造成至少 16 人死亡。 乌克兰一直依赖美国提供的爱国者拦截导弹，这些导弹用于对抗俄罗斯的弹道导弹，但由于伊朗战争，库存不足，导致乌克兰容易受到俄罗斯的攻击。 泽伦斯基曾表示，他...

reflection.en: The Kremlin adviser's veiled threat of "semi-military" responses against UK drone factories highlights the perilous path of escalating conflict. Jesus' warning in Matthew 26:52 reminds us that resorting to violence often begets more violence, trapping all involved in a destructive cycle. In a world where nations threaten to "draw the sword," this ancient...
reflection.zh: 克里姆林宫顾问对英国无人机工厂发出“半军事”回应的隐晦威胁，凸显了冲突升级的危险路径。雅伟耶稣在马太福音26:52中的警告提醒我们，诉诸暴力往往会招致更多的暴力，使所有卷入其中的人陷入破坏性的循环。在一个国家威胁要“拔刀”的世界里，这古老的智慧呼吁我们更深入地反思此类行动的长期后果。

title.en: NZ religious sect leader jailed over death of Chinese follower
title.zh: 新西兰宗教团体领袖因中国追随者死亡被判入狱

summary.en: A New Zealand court has sentenced religious sect leader Kaixiao Liu to over 10 years in prison for the manslaughter and kidnapping of 70-year-old Shulai Wang. Wang's body was found wrapped in rice bags near Auckland's Gulf Harbour in March 2024, after he had traveled from China to live with Liu's family.
summary.zh: 新西兰一家法院判处宗教团体领袖刘凯啸十年以上监禁，罪名是过失杀人和绑架70岁的王树来。王树来从中国前往新西兰与刘凯啸的家人同住后，其尸体于2024年3月在奥克兰海湾港附近被发现，当时被裹在米袋中。

body.en:
A New Zealand court has jailed a religious sect leader over the death of an elderly follower who had travelled from China to live with his family.

Kaixiao Liu was found guilty of manslaughter and kidnapping, and sentenced to more than 10 years in prison.

The body of 70-year-old Shulai Wang had been found wrapped in rice bags near Auckland's Gulf Harbour in March 2024, sparking a major homicide investigation which eventually led to Liu.

Liu, a musician who previously appeared in a talent show in China, had denied the charges. He also denied he is a cult leader and said he only attracted followers through his music.

During the trial the court heard that Wang had travelled from Hainan island in China to New Zealand in August 2023.

She moved in with Liu and his family at their house, which Liu had called "the Ark", along with several other female followers.

Prosecutors said that the women acted in "servitude" to Liu and his family, and their lives were tightly controlled by Liu, where they referred to him as "Lord" or "Master".

Wang reportedly spent her days taking care of Liu's children, studying scripture, and planting vegetables.

The court heard that Wang had struggled to comply with the strict rules, possibly due to her old age, and was frequently disciplined.

In March 2024, Wang tried to escape but was caught and restrained. She died later that day, the court heard.

The court heard that Liu, his family, and his followers dumped Wang's body near a marina at Gulf Harbour. Liu had taken his children along for the trip "as camouflage".

The body was found by a fisherman days later. Police eventually traced the rice bags used to wrap Wang's body to Liu, who had made unusually large purchases of that brand of rice.

Besides Liu, his wife, Lanyue Xiao, was sentenced to nearly eight years in jail for kidnapping and manslaughter, amongst other charges. His mother, Xiuyun Li and father, Jingui Liu, had earlier been convicted of kidnapping and misconduct to human remains and are due to be sentenced later this year.

On Tuesday's sentencing, Liu's lawyer asked for leniency arguing that his client feels remorse and "is not a cult leader, nor requires people to follow his cult", according to Radio New Zealand.

New Zealand media outlets reported that Liu had attended a military-based university in China.

In 2011, he was a contestant for China's Got Talent - clips posted online showed him singing onstage blindfolded.

Sometime in 2017, he moved to New Zealand along with Xiao, and the couple became permanent residents.

Liu attracted followers on Chinese social media where he posted religious discussions, video diaries, and clips of himself singing. He also set up a project called Universal Choir that produced cosmic-themed orchestral music.

body.zh: 新西兰一家法院因一名从中国前往与家人同住的老年信徒死亡而判处一名宗教教派领导人入狱。 刘凯晓犯故意杀人罪、绑架罪，被判处10年以上有期徒刑。 2024 年 3 月，70 岁的王舒来 (Shulai Wang) 的尸体在奥克兰海湾港附近被发现，尸体包裹在米袋中，引发了一项重大凶杀案调查，最终找到了刘。 曾参加过中国选秀节目的音乐家刘否认了这些指控。他还否认自己是邪教领袖，并表示他只是通过音乐吸引追随者。 法庭在庭审中获悉，王某于2023年8月从中国海南岛前往新西兰。 她和其他几名女追随者一起搬到了刘和他的家人的房子里，刘称之为“方舟”。 检察官称，这些妇女对刘及其家人构成“奴役”，她们的生活受到刘的严格控制，她们称刘为“主”或“师父”。 据报道，王每天都在照顾刘的孩子、学习经文和种植蔬菜。 法庭获悉，王可能由于年老，很难遵守严格的规定，并经常受到纪律处分。 2024年3月，王某试图逃跑，被抓获并束缚。法庭获悉，她当天晚些时候就去世了。 法庭获悉，刘及其家人和他的追随者将王的尸体丢弃在海湾港的一个码头附近。刘带着他的孩子们一起旅行“作为伪装”。 几天后，一名渔民发现了尸体。警方最终追踪到用于包裹王尸体的大米袋是刘，他购买了该品牌的大米，数量异常大。 除了刘之外，他的妻子肖兰月也因绑架和过失杀人等罪名被判处近八年监禁。他的母亲李秀云和父亲刘金贵早些时候被判犯有绑架和不当对待人体遗骸罪，并将于今年晚些时候被判刑。 据新西兰广播电台报道，在周二的宣判中，刘的律师请求宽大处理，理由是他的当事人感到悔恨，并且“不是邪教领袖，也不要求人们追随他的邪教”。 新西兰媒体报道称，刘曾就读于中国的一所军事大学。 2011年，他参加了《中国达人秀》，网上发布的视频显示他蒙着眼睛在舞台上唱歌。 2017年的某个时候，他和肖一起搬到了新西兰，夫妻俩成为了永久居民。 刘在中国社交媒体上吸引了粉丝，他在社交媒体上发布了宗教讨论、视频日记和自己唱歌的片段。他还建立了一个名为环球合唱团的项目，制作宇宙主题的管弦乐。 期间...

title.en: Trump's visa crackdown plan could affect thousands seeking asylum in the US
title.zh: 特朗普的签证打击计划可能影响数千名在美国寻求庇护者

summary.en: The US state department has declined to comment on the number of visas that may be revoked.
summary.zh: 美国国务院拒绝就可能被吊销的签证数量发表评论。

body.en:
The Trump administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum status in the United States.

If it happens, the move would be the largest single mass revocation of visas in US history and would likely face legal challenges.

Unless challenged or revised, the US state department is expected to announce in the coming weeks the revocation of so-called B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 whose holders have sought asylum or are now seeking asylum, according to state department documents obtained by the Associated Press (AP) and two US officials. The action will be taken in coordination with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

"We are coordinating with DHS to identify and revoke the nonimmigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the United States claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently," state department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said.

He declined to comment on the number of visas that might be revoked, saying "as the process will be ongoing, the number of revocations remains dynamic and will be done on a rolling basis".

The revocations would not necessarily result in their immediate deportation, the officials said. Most of those with asylum cases currently pending would be recategorised but would lose their status as business or tourism travellers, according to the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because the revocations are not final yet.

Since US President Donald Trump took office for his second term last year, his administration has steadily ramped up restrictions on visa applicants — demanding more information about their social media histories, requiring the posting of expensive bonds to process visas, and outright banning the issuance of visas to citizens of certain countries.

In a social media post on Tuesday, US deputy secretary of state Christopher Landau called out people who he said try to use tourist and business visas to get into the US and then apply for asylum.

"People in the US and all over the world are fed up with bogus asylum claims," Landau said in a post on X. "Asylum isn’t supposed to be a loophole to circumvent immigration law."

Landau cited the case of a Colombian citizen who came to the US in 2015 on a tourist visa and then applied for asylum.

B1 visas are generally issued for business trips and B2 visas are generally issued for tourism, family visits or medical care. It was not immediately clear from the documents or the officials how many of these visa holders are seeking or have sought asylum in...
body.zh: 特朗普政府正准备撤销多达20万名已在美国申请或目前正在寻求庇护身份的外国人的商务和旅游签证。 如果发生这种情况，此举将是美国历史上最大规模的单次大规模撤销签证，并可能面临法律挑战。 美联社和两名美国官员获得的国务院文件显示，除非受到质疑或修改，否则美国国务院预计将在未来几周内宣布撤销 2016 年至 2026 年期间签发的、已寻求庇护或正在寻求庇护的所谓 B1 和 B2 签证。该行动将与国土安全部（DHS）协调采取。 美国国务院发言人汤米·皮戈特 (Tommy Pigott) 表示：“我们正在与国土安全部协调，以查明并吊销那些声称是短期游客来美国但随后申请庇护以永久留在这里的外国人的非移民签证。” 他拒绝就可能被撤销的签证数量发表评论，并表示“由于这一过程将持续进行，撤销的数量仍然是动态的，并将滚动进行”。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 官员们表示，撤销并不一定会导致他们立即被驱逐出境。官员们表示，大多数目前正在审理中的庇护案件将被重新分类，但将失去商务或旅游旅行者的身份。由于撤销尚未最终，这些官员要求匿名。 自美国总统唐纳德·特朗普去年就任第二任期以来，他的政府稳步加强了对签证申请人的限制——要求他们提供更多有关社交媒体历史的信息，要求提交昂贵的债券来办理签证，并彻底禁止向某些国家的公民发放签证。 美国副国务卿克里斯托弗·兰道在周二的社交媒体帖子中点名了那些试图使用旅游和商务签证进入美国然后申请庇护的人。 兰道在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示：“美国和世界各地的人们都厌倦了虚假的庇护申请。庇护不应该成为规避移民法的漏洞。” 兰道引用了一名哥伦比亚公民的案例，该公民于2015年持旅游签证来到美国，然后申请庇护。 B1签证一般签发给商务旅行，B2签证一般签发给旅游、探亲或医疗。从文件或官员中尚不清楚这些签证持有者中有多少人正在寻求或已经寻求庇护......

title.en: 'Economic asphyxiation': US unveils sweeping new sanctions campaign in attempt to isolate Iran
title.zh: “经济窒息”: 美国公布全面新制裁，试图孤立伊朗

summary.en: The United States has announced a new campaign of sweeping sanctions against Iran, aiming for 'economic asphyxiation' to isolate the nation. This move comes six months into a war that has seen peace talks stall and the crucial Strait of Hormuz blocked.
summary.zh: 美国宣布对伊朗实施一项新的全面制裁行动，旨在通过“经济窒息”来孤立该国。此举发生在一场持续六个月的战争中，这场战争导致和平谈判陷入僵局，并阻塞了重要的霍尔木兹海峡。

body.en:
United States treasury secretary Scott Bessent has laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, expanding the US' secondary sanctions threats and warning of dire consequences for countries that do not join the campaign.

The announcement on Tuesday came almost six months into a war on Iran that has ground to a stalemate, with stalled peace talks and Iran blocking most traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz .

Bessent earlier said the US was declaring an "economic D-Day" on Iran, but his announcement named no specific countries beyond Iran and gave no timelines.

"Around the globe, our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," Bessent told journalists.

"We are going to hold everyone accountable, and this is economic asphyxiation of this regime."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

He added that countries not joining US sanctions would "share in the isolation" of Iran, and noted that US President Donald Trump was making phone calls to world leaders requesting they stop interactions with Iran.

The US treasury department said expanded secondary sanctions would target Iran's digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors.

It also issued new sanctions against 60 individuals, companies and vessels that allegedly aid Iran in oil revenue generation, weapons procurement and cyber operations.

The sanctions hit entities around the world, including in the United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and in Europe.

Bessent vowed that any entity "that facilitates money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US dollar system".

Iran had been dismissive of the threat of additional sanctions, and on Tuesday its economy minister predicted "another defeat" for the US on the economic front.

"We've been waiting for these plans for a long time, and the government is and was ready and has a two-year plan to manage these events," Ali Madanizadeh said.

In a post before the announcement, Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the latest US threats were an admission of military defeat.

Gharibabadi asked why, if the US had achieved its goals, "there is a need for 'the largest financial invasion in history' and the mobilization of 'all institutions and powers' of the United States!

Iran has weathered decades of crushing international sanctions, and before the war it continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China, and to evade sanctions through complex international financial networks.

title.en: Eurovision faces fresh scrutiny as the Netherlands withdraws over Gaza tensions
title.zh: 欧洲歌唱大赛因加沙紧张局势导致荷兰退出而面临新的审查

summary.en: The Netherlands has announced its withdrawal from next year's Eurovision Song Contest, citing that the event can no longer be considered neutral due to deep divisions over the Gaza war. The broadcaster stated that international conflicts are increasingly undermining the contest's neutral character, turning it into a...
summary.zh: 荷兰宣布退出明年的欧洲歌唱大赛，理由是鉴于加沙战争引发的深刻分歧，该赛事已无法保持中立。荷兰广播公司表示，国际冲突日益削弱了比赛的中立性，使其成为一个分裂的平台。

body.en:
The Netherlands will not participate in next year's Eurovision Song Contest, its broadcaster said on Monday, saying the event can "no longer be considered neutral" given divisions over the Gaza war.

"It is undeniable that international conflicts are increasingly affecting the Contest, undermining its neutral character. The Eurovision Song Contest has therefore become a platform for division," Taco Zimmerman, director-general of AVROTROS, said in a statement from the broadcaster.

The contest has recently been hit by a wave of boycotts over Israel's participation.

Earlier this month, organisers announced they were excluding any country involved in an armed conflict from hosting the competition.

"However, the recently announced changes ... do not provide sufficient confidence that the independent and neutral character of the Eurovision Song Contest has been restored," the AVROTROS statement said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Israel came close to winning the competition in both 2025 and 2026, ultimately finishing second on each occasion.

Next year's event, the world's biggest live televised music event, will take place on 15 May in Bulgaria's Black Sea city of Burgas.

It will be the first time that the Balkan nation hosts the contest, coming after Bulgarian singer Darina Yotova, known as Dara, won this year's contest in the Austrian capital Vienna with the catchy floor-filler "Bangaranga".

Since its launch in 1955, Eurovision has become the ultimate pop platform, catapulting Swedish icons ABBA to worldwide fame, as well as boosting the likes of Celine Dion, Cliff Richard and Olivia Newton-John.

The 2026 competition was watched by 131 million viewers, down 35 million on the year before after five countries boycotted it over Israel's participation.

The Netherlands, Iceland, Spain, Ireland and Slovenia all pulled out of the contest — with the latter three refusing to broadcast the show at all.

The Dutch took part in the very first Eurovision Song Contest back in 1956, and have won on five occasions.

The most recent winner was Duncan Laurence, whose song Arcade won the contest in 2019, going on to top charts globally.

It became the first Eurovision entry to reach one billion streams on Spotify, according to the Eurovision website.

The withdrawal is "painful as we would have very much liked to be part of the Contest again next year," Zimmerman said.

"As a public broadcaster, we remain committed to our values. They guide us in everything we do, even when that means stepping away from an event that is very close to our hearts," he added.

title.en: DR Congo peace roadmap: Will the fighting finally end?
title.zh: 刚果民主共和国和平路线图：战火能否最终平息？

summary.en: A new peace roadmap has been established for the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo following negotiations in Geneva. The plan aims to address the ongoing conflict, but significant disagreements regarding M23 rebels, Rwanda's involvement, and security concerns could still impede its progress.
summary.zh: 在日内瓦谈判后，刚果民主共和国东部地区制定了一项新的和平路线图。该计划旨在解决持续的冲突，但关于M23叛军、卢旺达的角色以及安全方面的重大分歧仍可能阻碍其进展。

body.en:
A new roadmap sets out the conditions toward peace in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). But disagreements over M23 rebels, Rwanda's role and security concerns remain, and could still derail the process.

Representatives of the Congolese government and the Rwanda-backed M23 rebel group agreed on a roadmap for peace after negotiations in Geneva.

It builds on the  US-brokered framework signed in Doha last year, and sets out steps and timelines for negotiations and implementation: a ceasefire monitoring mechanism is also due to receive support from the UN peacekeeping mission, MONUSCO.

The United States, Qatar, the African Union (AU) and Switzerland have all expressed their support for the process as brokers of the push for peace.

However, it is not a full peace plan with bindíng resolutions and terms; rather, many aspects of the push will still need to be fine-tuned.

The new diplomatic initiative could nevertheless be offering fresh hope following  years of bloody conflict in eastern DRC; fighting in the region has killed hundreds of civilians and displaced millions since 2022. The M23 rebel group continues to control large parts of North Kivu and South Kivu  — two provinces in eastern DRC that are highly coveted for their minerals.

As disagreements remain over key issues, doubts continue to cast a shadow  over the prospect of a lasting peace.

"There are likely to be many more bumps on the road — disagreements remain over issues including sanctions against M23, the release of detainees and the timing of political reforms. So this remains a very fragile commitment," Alex Vines, Africa program director at the European Council on Foreign Relations, told DW.

Conflict analyst Clifton Chifuwe, executive director of the Centre for Peace Research and Advocacy (CPRA), a local NGO that focuses on conflict management, agrees with that assessment, pointing to the presence of multiple armed groups in the area, the deep level of mistrust between DRC and Rwanda, and competition over eastern Congo's mineral wealth.

He believes that the biggest of the challenges across the board is to turn this roadmap into action. 

Chifuwe told DW that independent monitoring mechanisms and the involvement of all key stakeholders will be essential for any peace to hold.

Rwanda has repeatedly rejected accusations that it backs M23 rebels — though international groups maintain the view that the small neighboring nation is deeply entrechned in the conflict .

"Rwanda's good faith and its relationship with M23 is a really key consideration. Kigali's buy-in to any agreement and influence over M23 is key."

Rwandan President Paul Kagame's...
body.zh: 新的路线图规定了刚果民主共和国东部实现和平的条件。但围绕“3·23”叛军、卢旺达角色和安全问题的分歧仍然存在，并且仍可能使这一进程脱轨。 刚果政府和卢旺达支持的M23叛乱组织的代表在日内瓦谈判后就和平路线图达成一致。 它以去年在美国斡旋的多哈签署的框架为基础，规定了谈判和实施的步骤和时间表：停火监测机制也将得到联合国维和特派团联刚稳定团的支持。 美国、卡塔尔、非洲联盟 (AU) 和瑞士都作为推动和平的中间人表示支持这一进程。 然而，这并不是一个包含有约束力的决议和条款的完整和平计划；相反，推动的许多方面仍需要进行微调。 尽管如此，在刚果民主共和国东部经历了多年的血腥冲突之后，新的外交举措可能会带来新的希望；自 2022 年以来，该地区的战斗已造成数百名平民死亡，数百万人流离失所。M23 叛乱组织继续控制着北基伍和南基伍的大部分地区，这两个省份位于刚果民主共和国东部，矿产资源备受觊觎。 由于在关键问题上仍存在分歧，疑虑继续给持久和平的前景蒙上阴影。 欧洲外交关系委员会非洲项目主任亚历克斯·瓦恩斯（Alex Vines）对德国之声表示：“道路上可能会遇到更多坎坷——在制裁‘3·23’运动、释放被拘留者以及政治改革时机等问题上仍存在分歧。因此，这仍然是一个非常脆弱的承诺。” 冲突分析师克利夫顿·奇富韦 (Clifton Chifuwe) 是当地一家专注于冲突管理的非政府组织和平研究与宣传中心 (CPRA) 的执行主任，他同意这一评估，并指出该地区存在多个武装团体、刚果民主共和国和卢旺达之间根深蒂固的不信任，以及刚果东部矿产资源的竞争。 他认为，最大的挑战是将这一路线图转化为行动。 奇富韦告诉德国之声，独立的监督机制和所有主要利益攸关方的参与对于维持和平至关重要。 卢旺达一再否认其支持 M23 叛乱分子的指控，尽管国际组织仍然认为这个邻国小国深深卷入了冲突。 “卢旺达的诚意及其与 M23 的关系是一个真正关键的考虑因素。基加利对任何协议的支持以及对 M23 的影响力都是关键。” 卢旺达总统保罗·卡加梅...

Even with remaining disagreements over M23 rebels and Rwanda's role, the commitment to a process for peace reflects the spirit of those who strive to build bridges. Yahweh blesses those who actively seek to bring an...
reflection.zh: 刚果民主共和国东部地区在日内瓦谈判后达成的和平路线图，凸显了缔造和平这项充满挑战但至关重要的工作。尽管在M23叛军和卢旺达的角色问题上仍存在分歧，但致力于和平进程的承诺，体现了那些努力搭建桥梁者的精神。雅伟赐福那些积极寻求结束冲突、促进和解的人。

title.en: Iran protest victim: 'They were shooting to kill'
title.zh: 伊朗抗议受害者：‘他们是想杀人’

summary.en: DW spoke with several Iranians affected by a brutal crackdown at the hands of the Tehran's security forces during the height of massive public protests in January.
summary.zh: 德国之声采访了几位受一月份大规模公众抗议高潮期间德黑兰安全部队残酷镇压影响的伊朗人。

body.zh: 德国之声采访了几名受到德黑兰安全部队在一月份大规模公众抗议活动最激烈期间残酷镇压影响的伊朗人。 2026 年 1 月，就在美国和以色列对伊朗发动袭击的几周前，数千名伊朗人冒着生命危险参加了德黑兰政权有史以来规模最大、范围最广的公众起义。 由于对经济困难的不满，抗议活动于 2025 年 12 月开始，但范围和规模很快扩大。 由情报部、巴斯基民兵和伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）组成的政权安全部队在街头向抗议者开枪和殴打。 镇压的规模引起了国际社会的谴责。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普曾一度威胁要对该政权进行军事打击作为回应，并告诉抗议者“援助正在路上”。 但帮助始终没有到来。由于随后的战争给血腥镇压的后果蒙上了阴影，对伊朗公众挺身而出反对政权的支持从议程上消失了。 目前尚无 2026 年 1 月抗议活动中死伤人数的准确数字。伊朗当局估计死亡人数超过 3,100 人。 然而，国际特赦组织强调，由于抗议期间互联网被关闭、镇压规模以及受害者家属面临的压力，实际死亡人数可能要高得多。 总部位于美国的伊朗人权活动组织 (HRANA) 确认了 7,000 多人死亡，并对数千人进行了调查。 血腥镇压七个月后，受害者面临着永久性的身体残疾，同时失去了工作或接受教育的机会。 从伊朗境内获取信息既困难又危险，出于安全考虑，德国之声的采访伙伴选择使用化名。德国之声能够通过人权网络联系受害者。 一名抗议者马苏德在德黑兰郊外的一座城市的示威活动中被数百颗弹丸击伤，数月以来一直没有得到治疗，几天前被埋葬。 据不愿透露具体位置的亲属称，马苏德首先头部被弹丸击中。一名便衣警察随后向他的大腿开枪，并反复踢伤口，导致他的股骨从髋关节脱臼。 马苏德几个月来一直在与伤病作斗争。他的亲戚为他在家筹集治疗费用，他接受了多次手术，但感染不断复发和蔓延。马苏德在生命的最后几天拒绝接受进一步的治疗，他的兄弟说这让他为给家人带来“如此大的负担”而感到羞愧。 哈米德·赫马特普尔 (Hamid Hemmatpour) 是一名医生兼董事会...

reflection.en: The report of Tehran's security forces 'shooting to kill' unarmed protesters highlights the grave danger faced by a populace under oppressive rule. Proverbs 28:15 reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a predatory animal to a helpless people, causing immense suffering and fear. In such times, the human spirit longs for leaders who protect their citizens...
reflection.zh: 德国之声报道德黑兰安全部队“开枪杀人”手无寸铁的抗议者，凸显了民众在压迫性统治下所面临的严重危险。箴言28:15提醒我们，邪恶的统治者对无助的百姓来说，如同凶猛的野兽，带来巨大的痛苦和恐惧。在这样的时刻，人类灵魂渴望那些保护公民而非恐吓他们的领导者。

title.en: Myanmar: Why Rohingya refugees can't return
title.zh: 缅甸：罗兴亚难民为何无法回归

summary.en: Nine years after the Rohingya were driven from Myanmar, discussions about their repatriation from Bangladesh refugee camps have resumed. Myanmar has verified around 308,000 refugees but states they will not be repatriated until security conditions improve in Rakhine State.
summary.zh: 罗兴亚人被驱逐出缅甸九年后，关于他们从孟加拉国难民营遣返的讨论再次浮现。缅甸已核实了约30.8万名难民的身份，但表示在若开邦安全状况改善之前，不会遣返他们。

body.en:
Nine years after the Rohingya were driven from Myanmar, claims of progress on refugee returns have revived talk of repatriation.

Myanmar's military-backed government is again talking about bringing Rohingya refugees home from refugee camps in neighboring Bangladesh. 

Earlier this month, authorities in Naypyidaw, Myanmar's capital, said they had made progress verifying Rohingya refugees in  Bangladesh for possible repatriation.

Of the 820,000 names submitted by Bangladesh, Myanmar said it had verified around 308,000 as former residents but would not repatriate them until security conditions improve in civil war-torn Rakhine State.

But analysts told DW that large-scale, safe repatriation is now arguably further out of reach than at any point since 2017. Myanmar is engulfed in civil war, the military no longer controls most of Rakhine state , and the Rohingya are denied citizenship.

In August 2017, Myanmar's military launched sweeping operations in northern Rakhine state after alleged attacks by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) militant group on security posts.

More than 750,000 Rohingya, a long-persecuted Muslim ethnic minority in predominantly Buddhist Myanmar, fled to Bangladesh, joining hundreds of thousands displaced by earlier crackdowns.

Muslim-majority Bangladesh now hosts around 1.2 million Rohingya refugees, mostly in camps around the southern coastal district of Cox's Bazar, according to UN bodies.

Myanmar does not recognize the Rohingya as one of its 135 officially recognized ethnic groups and has long referred to them as "Bengalis," implying they are migrants from Bangladesh despite generations of Rohingya having lived in Rakhine.

UN investigators found evidence of genocidal intent by Myanmar's military, while the United States argued in 2022 that members of the military had committed genocide and crimes against humanity against the Rohingya.

A genocide case brought by the West African nation of Gambia against Myanmar remains before the International Court of Justice in The Hague.

Myanmar's 2021 coup triggered a nationwide civil war that is still raging, even after a much-criticized election earlier this year saw the formation of a civilian government, which remains dominated by officials from the military and junta .

"Safe repatriation is simply not possible," Ronan Lee, a researcher at Loughborough University and author of the 2021 book "Myanmar's Rohingya Genocide," told DW.

There is a civil war in Myanmar and the economy has collapsed, Lee said, meaning a return under present conditions would carry a high risk of the Rohingya facing violence from the military.

"Myanmar's government is dominated by the same military that genocidally deported the Rohingya in 2017," Lee added. "Life in Myanmar...
body.zh: 罗兴亚人被赶出缅甸九年后，难民回返方面取得进展的说法重新引发了有关遣返的讨论。 缅甸军方支持的政府再次讨论将罗兴亚难民从邻国孟加拉国的难民营带回家。 本月早些时候，缅甸首都内比都当局表示，他们在核实孟加拉国罗兴亚难民是否可能被遣返方面取得了进展。 缅甸表示，在孟加拉国提交的 82 万姓名中，已核实约 30.8 万人为前居民，但在饱受内战蹂躏的若开邦安全状况改善之前不会将他们遣返。 但分析人士告诉德国之声，大规模、安全的遣返现在可以说比2017年以来的任何时候都更加遥不可及。缅甸陷入内战，军队不再控制若开邦大部分地区，罗兴亚人被剥夺公民身份。 2017 年 8 月，在若开罗兴亚救世军 (ARSA) 激进组织据称袭击安全哨所后，缅甸军方在若开邦北部发起了扫荡行动。 超过 75 万罗兴亚人逃往孟加拉国，加入了因早期镇压而流离失所的队伍。罗兴亚人是缅甸佛教占主导地位的长期受迫害的穆斯林少数民族。 据联合国机构称，穆斯林占多数的孟加拉国目前收容了约 120 万罗兴亚难民，其中大部分居住在科克斯巴扎尔南部沿海地区周围的难民营中。 缅甸不承认罗兴亚人是其 135 个官方承认的民族之一，并且长期以来一直将他们称为“孟加拉人”，这意味着尽管罗兴亚人世代居住在若开邦，但他们是来自孟加拉国的移民。 联合国调查人员发现了缅甸军方有种族灭绝意图的证据，而美国则在 2022 年辩称，军方成员对罗辛亚人犯下了种族灭绝罪和反人类罪。 西非国家冈比亚针对缅甸提起的种族灭绝案件仍在海牙国际法院审理。 缅甸 2021 年的政变引发了一场仍在激烈进行的全国性内战，尽管在今年早些时候的一场备受批评的选举中组建了一个仍由军方和军政府官员主导的文职政府。 拉夫堡大学研究员、2021 年出版的《缅甸罗辛亚种族灭绝》一书的作者罗南·李 (Ronan Lee) 告诉德国之声：“安全遣返根本不可能。” 李说，缅甸正在发生内战，经济已经崩溃，这意味着在目前的情况下，罗辛亚人的回归将面临面临军方暴力的高风险。 “缅甸政府由 2017 年种族灭绝驱逐罗兴亚人的同一支军队主导，”李补充道。 “缅甸的生活...

In such prolonged displacement, Yahweh calls us to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves, advocating for justice and the rights of all who are vulnerable. We are...
reflection.zh: 罗兴亚人被驱逐出缅甸九年后，仍处于困境之中，82万名申请遣返者中只有一小部分得到核实，归家之路遥遥无期。在如此漫长的流离失所中，雅伟呼召我们为那些无法为自己发声的人说话，为所有弱势群体的正义和权利而倡导。这提醒我们，要为一切困苦之人开口，确保他们的困境在政治复杂性中不被遗忘。

title.en: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
title.zh: 科学家在颅骨骨髓中发现新的“免疫中心”

summary.en: In mouse skull marrow, 'immune hubs' that actively defend the brain have been discovered. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.
summary.zh: 在小鼠颅骨骨髓中，科学家发现了主动防御大脑的“免疫中心”。人类颅骨中也存在类似的细胞，但其作用尚不明确。

body.en:
In mouse skull marrow, 'immune hubs' that actively defend the brain have been discovered. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

The skull has traditionally been regarded largely as armor for the brain. New research from the United States  suggests it may have another role: proactively helping to defend what lies beneath it.

Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis identified previously unknown immune "security stations" in the bone marrow of mouse skulls.

The lymph node-like structures responded to brain tumors before more distant lymph nodes in the neck did. When researchers disrupted the structures in mice with glioblastoma, an aggressive brain cancer , the tumors grew faster and the animals died sooner.

"The skull should no longer be viewed simply as a protective shell around the brain," senior study author Jonathan Kipnis told DW.

"It contains specialized immune environments that appear capable of responding locally to changes within the brain."

The discovery, published in the journal "Nature," comes with an important caveat: The researchers have so far only demonstrated how the structures function in mice, not humans.

Kipnis cautioned that the human evidence remains preliminary: "We found similar immune cells in human skull marrow, suggesting that related structures may exist, but we have not yet demonstrated that they are organized or function in the same way as those in mice," he said.

For much of the 20th century, the brain was described as "immune privileged" — unusually protected from immune activity because inflammation that is useful elsewhere can damage delicate brain tissue.

The blood-brain barrier, which tightly controls what can pass from the bloodstream into brain tissue, reinforced the idea that the brain was largely isolated from the body's conventional immune system.

Researchers now know that the brain communicates continuously with the immune system, particularly through tissues surrounding the brain. 

Kipnis' lab helped drive that rethink in previous work, first by identifying lymphatic vessels in the membranes surrounding the brain and later by showing tiny channels connecting those membranes to the skull's bone marrow.

"The traditional concept of immune privilege has already changed substantially," Kipnis said. "Our findings add another layer by showing that specialized immune structures exist within the skull bone marrow, immediately adjacent to the brain."

The researchers tracked proteins moving from mouse brains through microscopic skull channels and into the bone marrow.

title.en: The challenge brewing behind the front lines in Ukraine
title.zh: 泽连斯基不希望乌克兰面临的“海啸”

summary.en: Ukraine hasn't held elections since Russia's full-scale invasion, but tensions have been brewing over the issue. President Zelenskyy has rebuffed calls for wartime elections, stating they would be a "tsunami for the state" and "split Ukraine."
summary.zh: 俄罗斯全面入侵以来，乌克兰一直没有举行选举，但围绕这一问题，紧张局势一直在酝酿。泽连斯基总统拒绝了战时选举的呼吁，称这将是“国家的灾难海啸”，并会“分裂乌克兰”。

body.en:
More than four years after Russia launched the full-scale invasion that has devastated Ukraine and claimed hundreds of thousands of lives, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is facing a new political challenge: whether to hold elections during wartime.

The issue emerged last week after former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov , who was recently dismissed from his role, called for Zelenskyy to find a way to hold elections while fighting was ongoing.

The move was seen as the biggest challenge to Zelenskyy's leadership since the invasion began in February 2022, with Zelenskyy rebuffing calls for a wartime election.

"Elections right now are a tsunami for the state, which will split Ukraine," he said on Sunday, local time.

"That's why my strategy is to steer the country toward an ending of the war and to preserve an independent and sovereign state."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

National elections have been suspended since the invasion began and polling shows most Ukrainians support delaying a vote until the fighting ends.

Zelenskyy won Ukraine's 2019 presidential election in a landslide and would have ordinarily served a five-year term.

After Russia launched its full-scale invasion, Ukraine introduced martial law, which suspends some civil liberties, including national elections.

Zelenskyy's presidential term expired in 2024, but he remained in office as Ukraine's constitutional and legal system provides for continuity of government during martial law. The country's parliament has also continued operating.

Fighting continues along a front line stretching more than 1,200km, while Ukrainian cities, including the capital Kyiv, remain under regular bombardment from Russian drones and missiles.

An election would potentially require millions of Ukrainians to travel to polling stations, creating security risks and raising concerns about how voting could be conducted safely.

Political parties would also need to campaign while the country remained under attack, while authorities would have to find a way for hundreds of thousands of soldiers serving on the front line to vote.

As of the end of June, more than 4.4 million Ukrainians had temporary protection status in the European Union, meaning Ukraine would have to organise hundreds of polling stations across Europe.

Nearly four million Ukrainians have also been internally displaced, making voter registration more difficult and potentially diverting resources from the war effort.

Then there are those living under Russian occupation unable to vote. Ukrainian officials estimated that, as of 2024, around 4.5 million adult Ukrainians remained in Russian-occupied territory.

title.en: Beyond China's humanoid robots, a quieter machine revolution is unfolding
title.zh: 除了中国的人形机器人之外，一场更安静的机器革命正在展开

summary.en: There are more than two million robots working in China's factories - and they are scaling up fast.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
His world certainly does. The 28-year-old keeps up with the latest technology by spending his spare time in factories that are switching to automation. That way he knows what to prioritise when teaching his class about artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics.

In front of him, around 30 college students are studying code. One of them is typing furiously as his eyes dart from the screen to the robot: "The idea is it will grab that cylindrical piece and move it over there."

A line of industrial robots are waiting to be programmed, and in another part of the classroom, students are trying to develop robotic medical instruments. As he guides them, Chen declares: "If you are not needed by the world of AI and robotics, then you'll definitely be among those eliminated".

For the people in this room, this is a step - or rather a leap - towards a future that China is meticulously building: Xi Jinping's $20bn (£14.7bn) plan to put his country at the forefront of innovation and in direct competition with the US.

The evidence is all around them. They are in the Hangzhou Technician Institute, one of several huge, purpose-built vocational schools that want to churn out the next generation of tech-savvy engineers. The campus sits on the outskirts of Hangzhou, a former imperial capital whose futuristic skyline is just the first hint of its role as a global tech hub.

Across the country, there are more than two million robots working in China's factories - which is more than anywhere else - and they are continuing to scale up at extraordinary speed.

It is a commitment that will surely change the world, much like the last time the Chinese economy underwent a massive transformation. It is already shipping its robots across the globe: more than half of the world's industrial robots are now made in China.

What is less clear is the impact of such sweeping automation in a country that sits at the heart of global manufacturing, trade and innovation. What does this mean for China's human workforce, for instance? And how would we be able to truly measure the cost of this transformation in a regime that controls information so tightly?

The future of China's workers is uncertain in the industrial revolution the world has been watching: gleaming solar grids, peak hours made noiseless by electric vehicles, machines that run faster than Usain Bolt. Over the weekend, China hosted the second edition of the World Humanoid Games where robots boxed, sprinted and marched.

What is fuelling this spectacle is another, less visible revolution happening inside factories and classrooms.

body.zh: 他的世界确实如此。这位 28 岁的年轻人将业余时间花在正在转向自动化的工厂里，以跟上最新技术的步伐。这样，他就知道在课堂上教授人工智能 (AI) 和机器人技术时要优先考虑什么。 在他面前，大约有 30 名大学生正在学习代码。其中一个人正在疯狂地打字，他的眼睛从屏幕扫向机器人：“我们的想法是，它会抓住那个圆柱形部件并将其移到那里。” 一排工业机器人正在等待编程，在教室的另一部分，学生们正在尝试开发机器人医疗仪器。在引导他们时，陈宣称：“如果人工智能和机器人世界不需要你，那么你肯定会被淘汰”。 对于在座的人们来说，这是中国正在精心建设的未来的一步，或者说是一次飞跃：习近平斥资 200 亿美元（147 亿英镑）的计划，旨在让中国走在创新的前沿，与美国直接竞争。 证据就在他们周围。他们就读于杭州技师学院，这是几所大型的专门职业学校之一，旨在培养下一代精通技术的工程师。该园区位于前帝国首都杭州的郊区，其未来主义的天际线只是其作为全球科技中心角色的第一个迹象。 在全国范围内，有超过 200 万台机器人在中国的工厂里工作——这比其他任何地方都多——而且它们还在以惊人的速度继续扩大规模。 这是一个必将改变世界的承诺，就像上次中国经济经历巨大转型一样。它已经将其机器人运送到全球各地：目前世界上一半以上的工业机器人是在中国制造的。 不太清楚的是，如此全面的自动化对一个处于全球制造、贸易和创新中心的国家产生的影响还不太清楚。例如，这对中国的劳动力意味着什么？在一个如此严格控制信息的政权中，我们如何才能真正衡量这种转变的成本？ 在全世界都在关注的工业革命中，中国工人的未来充满不确定性：闪闪发光的太阳能电网、电动汽车让高峰时段变得无噪音、运行速度比尤塞恩·博尔特还快的机器。周末，中国主办了第二届世界人形运动会，机器人进行了拳击、短跑和行军比赛。 推动这一奇观的是工厂和教室里发生的另一场不太明显的革命。 BBC 参观了工业现场，在那里我们看到了机器人，它们看起来不像人类，在舞台上跳舞或跳跃，但可以焊接、油漆、举升、组装和昼夜不停地工作……

body.en: Two activists who organised commemorations of the bloody crackdown on China’s 1989 pro-democracy protests now face jail. Remembering is not a crime For decades, Hong Kong mourned when the mainland could not. Its huge annual Tiananmen vigil kept alive the memory of the 1989 pro-reform protests in Beijing, and of the massacre that suppressed them. Along with Macau, it was the only place in China where the anniversary could be publicly marked and the truth preserved. But the crackdown on the 2019 uprising in Hong Kong has crushed the freedoms that the region once enjoyed. That year’s vigil was the last. On Friday, two leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance, which organised the commemoration, were convicted of incitement to subversion under the draconian national security law. title.en: China probes use of formaldehyde to keep cabbages fresh
title.zh: 中国调查使用甲醛保鲜白菜事件

summary.en: Chinese authorities have launched an investigation into reports of formaldehyde, a prohibited carcinogen, being used to preserve cabbages for human consumption. The footage, verified by officials in Hebei province, shows individuals dipping cabbages in a solution before loading them for transport. China is the world's...
summary.zh: 中国当局已对有关使用甲醛（一种被禁的致癌物质）保鲜供人食用的白菜的报道展开调查。河北省官员证实，他们已核实了显示有人将白菜浸入溶液中，然后装车运输的视频。中国是世界上最大的白菜生产国。

body.en:
Authorities in China have launched an investigation into reports of formaldehyde being used to preserve the freshness of cabbages for human consumption.

Officials in the north-eastern Hebei province confirmed that they had verified footage showing individuals dipping cabbages in a solution before loading them onto trucks for transportation.

An environmental blogger first released the footage last week. Using formaldehyde, a colourless chemical used for preserving biological specimens that is known to cause cancer, for keeping food fresh is strictly prohibited in China.

China is the world's largest producer of cabbages, most of which are exported to neighbouring countries in Asia.

Police have taken legal action against the individuals involved, according to state media.

Officials are now moving swiftly to prevent panic and restore confidence by carrying out spot checks on markets across the country.

Chinese state media says investigators will also establish how widespread the practice is and take measures to trace affected vegetables.

Local authorities in Kangbao county said in a statement issued on Saturday: "Any illegal or non-compliant practices discovered will be dealt with strictly in accordance with the law to ensure the safety of the vegetable supply."

Xinfadi market in Beijing, one of the major sources of fresh produce in the capital, issued a statement saying that it had investigated the source of its cabbages, adding that none of the affected vegetables had entered its market.

An editorial in the People's Daily wrote: "The wholesalers focused solely on their immediate economic interests while completely disregarding the lives and health of consumers. [They] crossed a legal red line and breached the moral bottom line."

China produces well over 30 million tonnes of cabbages each year, nearly half of the world's annual total. Vietnam, South Korea and Russia are among the largest export destinations for the vegetable.

Exposure to relatively high quantities of formaldehyde in some workplaces has been linked to some types of cancer in humans, but the effect of exposure to small amounts is less clear, according to the American Cancer Society.
body.zh: 中国当局已对有关使用甲醛来保鲜供人类食用的卷心菜的报道展开调查。 河北省东北部的官员证实，他们已经核实了一段视频，显示人们将卷心菜浸入溶液中，然后装上卡车进行运输。 一位环保博主上周首次发布了这段视频。中国严格禁止使用甲醛（一种用于保存生物样本的无色化学物质，已知会致癌）来保鲜食物。 中国是世界上最大的卷心菜生产国，大部分出口到亚洲邻国。 据官方媒体报道，警方已对涉案人员采取法律行动。 官员们现在正在迅速采取行动，通过对全国市场进行抽查来防止恐慌并恢复信心。 中国官方媒体称，调查人员还将确定这种做法的普遍程度，并采取措施追踪受影响的蔬菜。 康保县当地政府在周六发布的一份声明中表示：“对发现的违法违规行为，将依法严肃处理，确保蔬菜供应安全。” 北京新发地市场是首都生鲜农产品的主要来源之一，该市场发表声明称，已对大白菜的来源进行调查，并补充说，受影响的蔬菜尚未进入该市场。 《人民日报》的一篇社论写道：“批发商只顾眼前的经济利益，完全不顾消费者的生命健康。他们跨越了法律红线，突破了道德底线。” 中国每年生产超过3000万吨的卷心菜，几乎占世界年产量的一半。越南、韩国和俄罗斯是蔬菜最大的出口目的地之一。 据美国癌​​症协会称，在某些工作场所接触相对较高含量的甲醛与人类某些类型的癌症有关，但接触少量甲醛的影响尚不清楚。

reflection.en: The news of formaldehyde being used to preserve cabbages in Hebei province is a stark reminder of how easily trust can be broken in commerce. Yahweh's word reminds us that "a false balance is an abomination to Yahweh, but a just weight is his delight," emphasizing the importance of integrity and honesty in all dealings. This incident underscores the need...
reflection.zh: 河北省使用甲醛保鲜白菜的消息，严峻地提醒我们商业中信任是多么容易被破坏。雅伟的话语提醒我们：“诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶，公平的法码为他所喜悦”，强调了在所有交易中诚信的重要性。这一事件凸显了以公众福祉为先，而非追求欺骗性利益的道德实践的必要性。

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.
verse.textZh: 诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶；公平的法码为他所喜悦。

title.en: 'Can't abstain from this debate': Pacific nations the next frontier in deep-sea mining
title.zh: “无法回避的辩论”：太平洋国家成为深海采矿的下一个前沿

summary.en: A new report warns that commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin as early as 2027, driven by increasing rivalry between the United States and China for critical minerals. Pacific nations are reportedly split between the promise of economic benefits and the risk of irreversible damage to the environment...
summary.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国之间对关键矿产的竞争日益加剧，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能最早在2027年开始。据报道，太平洋国家在经济利益的承诺与对环境和当地生计造成不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。

body.en:
Commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin in months without policy guardrails due to increasing rivalry between the United States and China over critical minerals, a new report warns.

Analysis by the Lowy Institute has found mining could start as early as 2027, with the floor of the Pacific Ocean holding vast quantities of prized resources.

The contest between the world's two biggest economies is being driven by demand created by batteries, weapons systems, and power grids.

The region's nations are split between the promise of economic spoils and the risk of irreversible damage to the ecosystem, fisheries, food security, livelihoods and culture, according to the research.

It argues the absence of an international governance framework for commercial deep-sea mining leaves Pacific states negotiating without internationally agreed protections.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

This also leaves them dependent on individual agreements drafted by companies seeking to mine their ocean floor.

"For the Pacific Island nations caught in the middle of this great power battle for critical mineral supremacy, the economic proposition is difficult to refuse," the Lowy Institute's Connor Graham writes.

"The problem is not that Pacific nations disagree, it is that they are being forced to negotiate individually against parties with vastly more resources, information, and legal capacity, and that the international framework designed to protect them has stalled."

Graham said while Australia was yet to take a clear position on deep-sea mining in the Pacific, it has the standing, relationships, and institutional presence to make an impact.

This includes its membership in the Pacific Islands Forum and as a long-standing ally of the US.

"A commitment to standards that have not been written as a condition for activity that is about to begin is less of a policy, and more of an abstention," he said.

Countries including Australia have started to enter into deals for critical minerals, which are crucial for a number for emerging technologies.

The federal government has announced a $1.2 billion critical minerals strategic reserve to secure the supply of key minerals deemed crucial for Australia's economy and national security.

For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter .
body.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国在关键矿产方面的竞争日益激烈，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能会在没有政策保护的情况下在几个月内开始。 洛伊研究所的分析发现，采矿最早可能在 2027 年开始，太平洋海底蕴藏着大量珍贵资源。 全球最大的两个经济体之间的竞争是由电池、武器系统和电网产生的需求驱动的。 研究表明，该地区各国在经济收益的承诺和生态系统、渔业、粮食安全、生计和文化遭受不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。 它认为，商业深海采矿国际治理框架的缺乏导致太平洋国家在没有国际商定保护的情况下进行谈判。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这也使得它们依赖于寻求海底采矿的公司起草的单独协议。 洛伊研究所的康纳·格雷厄姆写道：“对于陷入这场争夺关键矿产霸权的大国战争的太平洋岛国来说，这个经济提议很难拒绝。” “问题不在于太平洋国家不同意，而在于它们被迫与拥有更多资源、信息和法律能力的各方进行单独谈判，而旨在保护它们的国际框架已经陷入停滞。” 格雷厄姆表示，虽然澳大利亚尚未对太平洋深海采矿采取明确立场，但它拥有产生影响的地位、关系和机构存在。 这包括它是太平洋岛屿论坛的成员以及美国的长期盟友。 他说：“对尚未作为即将开始的活动条件的标准的承诺与其说是一项政策，不如说是一种弃权。” 包括澳大利亚在内的国家已开始签订关键矿物交易，这对许多新兴技术至关重要。 联邦政府宣布设立 12 亿美元的关键矿产战略储备，以确保对澳大利亚经济和国家安全至关重要的关键矿产的供应。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: The prospect of deep-sea mining in the Pacific presents a stark choice for island nations, balancing potential economic gains against the risk of irreversible ecological damage. As the report warns of mining commencing without adequate policy guardrails, the words of 1 Corinthians 10:23 remind us that while many actions may be permissible, not all are truly...
reflection.zh: 太平洋深海采矿的前景给岛屿国家带来了严峻的选择，需要在潜在的经济收益与不可逆转的生态破坏风险之间取得平衡。正如报告警告，在缺乏充分政策保障的情况下，采矿可能即将开始，哥林多前书10:23提醒我们，虽然许多事情是合法的，但并非所有事情都有益处或能造就人。这种情况呼唤智慧，以辨别什么能真正造就社区并保护雅伟的创造，而不是仅仅追求权宜之计。

verse.textEn: "I have the right to do anything," you say — but not everything is beneficial. "I have the right to do anything" — but not everything is constructive.
verse.textZh: 凡事都可行，但不都有益处；凡事都可行，但不都造就人。

title.en: Sam was jailed for helping Hong Kong's protesters. He came home to a city in silence
title.zh: 香港镇压异见，山姆出狱后发现城市一片寂静

summary.en: Six years after China imposed the National Security Law, Hong Kong's crackdown on dissent has spread beyond its borders.
summary.zh: 中国实施《国家安全法》六年之后，香港对异见的镇压已蔓延至境外。

body.en:
Watch Dateline’s latest episode, Hong Kong: A City Silenced, on 25 August at 9.30pm AEST on SBS or SBS On Demand.

At 21, Sam Chan Chi-sum was preparing to leave Hong Kong to continue his studies overseas.

He'd been involved with a student activist group that collected sweets and toiletries to send to people jailed after Hong Kong’s 2019 anti-government protests.

Authorities accused the group of using the supplies to build support among prisoners and incite opposition to the government.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In September 2021, Sam was arrested under Hong Kong’s sweeping National Security Law, which had been passed a year earlier, and was convicted of "subversion with the intent of overthrowing the government".

"Prison was awful. I shared a cell with around twenty people. At its most crowded, there could be forty of us," he said.

He alleged some prison officers purposely mistreated inmates associated with the protest movement.

"I don't know whether they were acting out of personal conviction or following orders. But they certainly made life difficult for us."

Two years after his release from prison, Sam is trying to rebuild a normal life.

He had dreamt of becoming a teacher or a nurse, but his criminal record prevents him from pursuing either career.

"Since being released from prison, I feel as though I've entered a much larger cell," he said.

Instead, he is training to become a documentary filmmaker, determined, he says, to capture the transformation of Hong Kong.

"Whatever the outcome for Hong Kong, whether the future is good or bad, I want to stay here and witness the changes that lie ahead."

Sam’s story is like many other young Hongkongers whose lives have been upended by China’s crackdown on freedoms in Hong Kong, a city once known for its outspoken press, independent judiciary and political opposition.

In 1997, after more than 150 years of British rule, Hong Kong was handed back to China under the "one country, two systems" arrangement that promised Hong Kong would keep a high degree of autonomy.

Like Sam, Carmen Lau was from a generation that came of age after this handover to China: neither British, nor truly Chinese.

As a teenager, Carmen led a student movement in her secondary school against the Chinese Communist Party's (CCP) attempt to introduce 'patriotism' lessons in Hong Kong schools.

Many Hongkongers feared it would promote the CCP’s version of patriotism in their city.

"That time was the first time that I was really involved in a social event," said Lau, who’s now 30 and lives in exile in London.

Following large demonstrations, the CCP abandoned its plans...
body.zh: 8 月 25 日晚上 9 点半（澳大利亚东部标准时间）在 SBS 或 SBS On Demand 观看《Dateline》的最新一集《香港：一座沉默的城市》。 21岁的陈志森正准备离开香港到海外继续深造。 他曾参与一个学生活动团体，该团体收集糖果和洗漱用品，寄给香港 2019 年反政府抗议活动后入狱的人。 当局指责该组织利用这些物资在囚犯中赢得支持并煽动反对政府。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 2021年9月，Sam根据一年前通过的香港国家安全法被捕，并被判“颠覆国家政权罪”。 “监狱太糟糕了。我和大约二十个人同住一间牢房。最拥挤的时候，我们可能有四十个人，”他说。 他声称一些监狱官员故意虐待与抗议运动有关的囚犯。 “我不知道他们是出于个人信念还是奉命行事。但他们确实让我们的生活变得困难。” 出狱两年后，萨姆正在努力重建正常的生活。 他曾梦想成为一名教师或护士，但他的犯罪记录阻止了他从事这两种职业。 “自从出狱后，我感觉自己好像进入了一个更大的牢房，”他说。 相反，他正在接受培训，成为一名纪录片制片人，他说，决心捕捉香港的转变。 “无论香港的结果如何，无论未来是好还是坏，我都想留在这里，见证未来的变化。” 萨姆的故事就像许多其他香港年轻人一样，他们的生活因中国对香港自由的镇压而被打乱。这座城市曾经以其直言不讳的新闻界、独立的司法机构和政治反对派而闻名。 1997年，在英国统治150多年之后，香港在“一国两制”安排下回归中国，并承诺香港将保持高度自治。 和 Sam 一样，刘嘉敏也是中国回归后长大的一代人：既不是英国人，也不是真正的中国人。 青少年时期，卡门在中学领导了一场学生运动，反对中国共产党试图在香港学校引入“爱国主义”课程。 许多香港人担心这会在他们的城市宣扬中共版本的爱国主义。 “那次是我第一次真正参与社交活动，”现年 30 岁、流亡伦敦的刘说。 大规模示威后，中共放弃了计划……

reflection.en: The story of Sam returning to a silenced city after imprisonment highlights the profound impact of oppressive rule on a community. Yahweh's word reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a roaring lion, bringing fear and helplessness to the people. In such times, we are called to remember the dignity of every individual and pray for justice and peace.
reflection.zh: 山姆在被囚禁后回到一个寂静的城市，这个故事凸显了压迫性统治对一个社区的深远影响。雅伟的话语提醒我们，邪恶的统治者如同咆哮的狮子，给人民带来恐惧和无助。在这样的时刻，我们被呼召要记住每个人的尊严，并为公义与和平祷告。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Watch: Moment humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's 100m record
title.zh: 观看：人形机器人打破尤塞恩·博尔特 100 米纪录的时刻

summary.en: The robot ran the distance in 9.39 seconds at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A robot has outperformed humans by running faster than Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record at the World Humanoid Robot Games in China.

The humanoid robot, developed by the Beijing Innovation Centre of Humanoid Robotics, ran the distance in 9.39 seconds at the event.

Eight-time Olympic gold medallist Bolt set the world record for humans in 2009, running 100m in 9.58 seconds.

The robot beat two others including one made by Chinese smartphone maker Honor - which the manufacturer says ran the distance in 9.32 seconds in a test run.

Other events at the robot games, which started on Saturday, include boxing and football, but also household tasks such as folding laundry.
body.zh: 在中国举行的世界人形机器人运动会上，机器人跑得比尤塞恩·博尔特 (Usain Bolt) 保持的 1 亿米短跑世界纪录还要快，从而超越了人类。 由北京仿人机器人创新中心研发的仿人机器人在比赛中跑出了9.39秒的成绩。 八届奥运会金牌得主博尔特在 2009 年以 9.58 秒跑完 100m 的成绩创造了人类世界纪录。 该机器人击败了另外两个机器人，其中包括中国智能手机制造商荣耀制造的一个机器人，该制造商表示，该机器人在测试运行中仅用了 9.32 秒就跑完了距离。 周六开始的机器人比赛的其他项目包括拳击和足球，还有叠衣服等家务活。

title.en: After two decades, China is preparing its boldest Moon mission yet
title.zh: 二十年后，中国正在准备迄今为止最大胆的月球任务

summary.en: China's ambitious space program will take it to the moon as soon as next month, and it's looking for water.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
How do you explore a place where the sun never shines? China's space program will soon embark on one of the most innovative lunar exploration missions in recent years.

We’ve known for nearly two decades that some form of water exists on the moon. What we still don’t know is exactly how much accessible water ice lies inside permanently shadowed craters, how deeply it is buried or what form it takes.

What we do know is that accessing that water ice will be a real challenge: it is found at the bottom of deep, hard-to-traverse craters where the sun never shines, remaining untouched for billions of years at temperatures well below –200C. These are among the most valuable places on the moon, but the hardest to reach and explore.

Lunar exploration has come a long way since the Soviet Union’s Luna-1 probe reached the moon's vicinity in January 1959. The Apollo missions and their successors showed the challenge is no longer simply to reach the moon. It is to explore places human and conventional rovers cannot easily go, and ultimately determine whether the moon itself can provide some of the resources that future explorers will need.

China has spent two decades building an increasingly ambitious lunar exploration program, named after Chang'e, the ancient Chinese goddess of the moon. The Chang'e-7 mission is expected to set course for our celestial neighbour later this month, although a recent failure involving a different Chinese rocket has introduced some uncertainty over the launch date. Here’s what makes this latest mission so interesting.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The mission will test several novel approaches to lunar exploration. It will consist of an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper.

In addition, the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite is already in place. Launched separately in March 2024, it subsequently supported the Chang'e-6 mission and will facilitate communication between Earth and the lunar surface during the Chang'e-7 mission.

We don’t know precisely where the mission will land, but a site on or near an illuminated ridge close to the Shackleton crater in the Lunar South Pole’s Aitken region is a prime candidate.

The hopper will be the mission’s real star. Unlike a wheeled rover, it’s designed to leap over broken terrain and descend into craters where sunlight never reaches, places conventional vehicles may simply be unable to enter.

Adding it to the mission makes sense, given the steep crater walls, broken terrain, permanent shadow and the need for autonomous navigation and communications.

body.zh: 如何探索一个阳光照不到的地方？中国的太空计划很快将启动近年来最具创新性的月球探测任务之一。 近二十年来，我们已经知道月球上存在某种形式的水。我们仍然不知道的是，在永久阴影的陨石坑内到底有多少可接近的水冰，它埋藏的深度有多深，或者它的形式是什么。 我们所知道的是，获取这些水冰将是一个真正的挑战：它是在难以穿越的深坑底部发现的，那里的阳光永远不会照射到，在远低于零下200摄氏度的温度下数十亿年都保持不变。这些是月球上最有价值的地方，但也是最难到达和探索的地方。 自 1959 年 1 月苏联的 Luna-1 探测器到达月球附近以来，月球探索已经取得了长足的进步。阿波罗任务及其后续任务表明，挑战不再仅仅是到达月球。它是为了探索人类和传统漫游车无法轻易到达的地方，并最终确定月球本身是否可以提供未来探险者所需的一些资源。 中国花了二十年的时间制定了一项日益雄心勃勃的月球探测计划，该计划以中国古代月亮女神嫦娥的名字命名。嫦娥七号任务预计将于本月晚些时候飞往我们的天体邻居，尽管最近另一枚中国火箭的失败给发射日期带来了一些不确定性。这就是这个最新任务如此有趣的原因。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 该任务将测试几种月球探索的新方法。它将由轨道飞行器、着陆器、漫游车和漏斗组成。 此外，鹊桥二号月球中继卫星也已就位。它于2024年3月单独发射，随后支持嫦娥六号任务，并将在嫦娥七号任务期间促进地球与月球表面之间的通信。 我们不知道任务将在哪里着陆，但月球南极艾特肯地区靠近沙克尔顿陨石坑的照明山脊上或附近的一个地点是主要候选地点。 漏斗将成为这次任务的真正明星。与轮式漫游车不同，它的设计目的是跳过破碎的地形并下降到阳光永远无法到达的陨石坑中，而传统车辆可能根本无法进入这些地方。 考虑到陡峭的火山口壁、破碎的地形、永久的阴影以及自主导航和通信的需求，将其添加到任务中是有意义的。 中国科学家不会寻找水的迹象；而是寻找水的迹象。我们...
